Red Delicious and Royal Delicious apple: growing guide for India

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Royal Delicious and Red Delicious are the standard, vigorous Delicious apples that most traditional Indian orchards are built on. They need 1,000–1,500 chilling hours (about 5,500–7,500 ft) and a compatible pollinizer, and they are prone to severe alternate bearing.

Red / Royal Delicious
Tree habit and fruitStandard, vigorous; striped or blushed red
Chilling need1,000–1,500 hours below 7°C (about 5,500–7,500 ft)
Role in the orchardMain variety; needs a pollinizer
StrengthsThe classic Indian apple with the familiar aroma; still the base of most old orchards in Himachal and Kashmir.
WeaknessesSevere alternate bearing (heavy one year, little the next) and weak colour at lower altitudes.

Most of the alternate-bearing and small-fruit complaints in old Delicious orchards come from too many fruits in an 'on' year. Thinning to one king fruit per cluster within 10–25 days after petal fall, plus the October urea, zinc and boron spray, are the two steps that break the cycle. See alternate bearing and fruit size.

At lower belts (4,500–6,000 ft) the newer spur and high-colour strains colour better than old Royal Delicious. See spur and high-colour strains.

Rootstock, spacing and feeding

Choose the rootstock by soil, not by variety alone: M.9 only on deep, fertile, irrigated land with a trellis; MM.106 only on well-drained soil; MM.111 on drier slopes (rootstock guide). Feed by tree age with our apple fertilizer calculator.

Pollination

Keep 25–33% compatible pollinizers flowering at the same time, 4–6 beehives per hectare at bloom, a boron spray at pink bud, and no sprays during full bloom.

Compare: all apple varieties and rootstocks.

Questions farmers ask

How much chilling does Red / Royal Delicious need?

1,000–1,500 hours below 7°C (about 5,500–7,500 ft).

Does Red / Royal Delicious need a pollinizer?

Main variety; needs a pollinizer.

What are the problems with Red / Royal Delicious?

Severe alternate bearing (heavy one year, little the next) and weak colour at lower altitudes.
